newsitem.title: JAPAN: RUBBER - Japan prices seen rising after spot expiry.
newsitem.headline: RUBBER - Japan prices seen rising after spot expiry.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures prices are likely to recover next week as downward pressure stemming from weakness in the spot contract disappears after the spot expiry on Friday, rubber traders said.
The spot July contract expired at 91.1 yen per kg at midday Friday, with 442 lots of deliveries.
Long liquidation in spot July ahead of its expiry had been weighing down the market in the past weeks.
"With a bearish factor now gone, I expect prices to recover next week," a rubber analyst at a commodity brokerage house in Tokyo said.
Benchmark December rubber on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange ended the morning session at 119.0 yen per kg on Friday, against Thursday's close of 118.5 yen.
On the Kobe Rubber Exchange, benchmark December rubber was quoted at 118.8 yen against 117.7 at the Thursday close.
Japanese traders expressed mixed feelings towards Thailand's decision on Thursday to extend the government rubber intervention scheme but to default on taking delivery of 23,100 tonnes of rubber.
"The news (about Thailand) was both bearish and bullish at the same time," a trader at another commodity broker said.

Thailand's Deputy Prime Minister Sukhawich Rangsitphol, who chairs the natural rubber policy committee, said on Thursday that the government expected to spend three billion baht in the next three months to prop up rubber prices in the domestic market.
But he also said the government will not take delivery of 23,100 tonnes of rubber to trim losses.
The rubber was purchased at around 109.00 U.S. cents a kg, while rubber prices have now fallen to 95-98 cents a kg.
The Japanese rubber market is expected to be supported later this year by growth in rubber output for automobile tyres, traders said.
The Japan Automobile Tyre Manufacturers' Association on Thursday revised upwards its forecast of Japan's rubber output for tyres in 1997 on expectations of growth in the country's car exports.

The group said Japan's rubber output for tyres in calendar 1997 is likely to total 1.105 million tonnes, up from an earlier forecast of 1.060 million tonnes. The revised figures represent a three percent increase from actual output in 1996.
It said the yen's weaker tendency against the dollar would push up Japan's automobile exports, creating greater rubber demand for tyres.
Thai rubber offer prices to Japan were at 96.00 U.S. cents per kg on an fob basis on Friday, against 95.00 U.S. cents on July 18.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 121.0 yen per kg as of Friday, against 120.0 yen a week ago.
